name: Salesmessage
summary: Business texting and SMS marketing in one shared inbox. Reach customers where they actually reply with two-way texting, automation and team collaboration.
best_for: sales and service teams that want two-way texting and calling in one CRM-linked inbox, and can estimate their monthly credit burn, messages plus call minutes, before they sign
skip_if: your audience doesn't respond to SMS, or your volume is low enough that the fixed 10DLC overhead outweighs the sending. Also skip it if you need a lot of seats cheaply. And skip it if your volume is small: since November 2026 the entry tier is $33 a month for 500 credits, roughly 250 two-credit messages
honest_knock: Two things cost money here. First, calling runs on the same meter as texting (1 credit a minute, 2 a minute when forwarding), so voice minutes eat the allowance you budgeted for messages. Second, the price went up in November 2026: Basic was merged into Pro and the 500-credit entry tier is now $33 a month, up from $25, with 10,000 credits at $450, up from $329 (read 23 November 2026). An MMS is 2 credits, so one picture message to 1,000 contacts is 2,000 credits: four times the entry allowance. Seats and numbers bill on top of every tier beyond the first of each: a five-person team on one number is $40 a month over the sticker, and the annual figures are per-month displays of a bill charged yearly. There is no published per-credit overage rate, so what happens when you run out mid-cycle is not stated where you buy: ask before you commit. And US business texting carries a regulatory layer of its own: 10DLC registration and carrier surcharges bill separately from anything quoted here, and opt-in and opt-out handling stays your legal responsibility: the platform enables compliance, it does not absolve you.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro (500 message credits a month) · billed monthly
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-23 on www.salesmessage.com/pricing, both billing modes, from the page's own tier data; earlier reads 8 August, 10 September, 13 October and 13 November 2026) Repriced since our 13 November reading. The Basic plan is gone: the page's own code says Basic is merged into Pro, so there is one self-serve plan, Pro, plus Enterprise, metered in message credits. A credits dropdown sets the price of Pro. Billed monthly: 500 credits a month $33, 1,000 $61, 2,500 $122, 5,000 $233, 7,500 $339 and 10,000 $450, then in 5,000-credit steps $650, $844, $1,028, $1,194, $1,356, $1,500, $1,633 and $1,756 for 50,000 credits a month. Annual billing is two months free: each tier costs ten times its monthly price for the year, so $330 for 500 credits a month (shown as $28 a month), $4,500 for 10,000 and $17,560 for 50,000. Against 13 November every step we can compare rose: 500 credits from $25 to $33 (+32%), 5,000 from $179 to $233 (+30%), 10,000 from $329 to $450 (+37%) and 50,000 from $1,499 to $1,756 (+17%). Enterprise is contact-for-pricing with custom credits, seats and numbers. Seats and numbers are still priced apart from the plan: the first seat is free and each additional seat is $10.00 a month or $100.00 a year; the first number is free and each additional number is $5.00 a month or $50.00 a year. The page defines the meter itself: SMS is 1 credit per 160 characters, MMS is 2 credits, calling is 1 credit a minute and call forwarding is 2 credits a minute. A 14-day free trial runs, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered, refunded less the message credits used. When we tried to sign up on 18 November 2026, the registration page required a credit card and a US mobile number before the account opened, under the line 'Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month'; on the 23 November ladder $61 is the monthly price of the 1,000-credit tier. We entered nothing and stopped there. The page publishes no per-credit overage rate, nor terms for taxes, carrier fees or country availability, so we quote none.

Stop: nothing was filled in and nothing was started, so no account was opened and no trial began. The core function, the text message inbox and the credit use per message, was therefore not tested. sessions.what: We opened the registration page of Salesmsg on 18 November 2026 and our AI assistant noted what it showed. Before an account opened, the page required a credit card and a US mobile number, although the button read Start my free trial with the line Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month above it. Nothing was filled in, so no account or trial started and we could not use the product. We never enter a card in a test.
findings: The button on the registration page read Start my free trial, but the page required a credit card and a US mobile number before an account opened. The 14-day trial is free and nothing is charged until it ends, but a card and a US mobile number come first. Salesmsg told us on 25 November 2026 that this is intentional: it sends on US carrier networks, and the checks keep spam and fraud signups out.

The line above the button said Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month. We did not record which plan the $61 belongs to and no checkout screen was reached. On the pricing ladder we read on 23 November 2026, $61 a month is the 1,000-credit Pro tier; the entry tier is $33 a month for 500 credits. So $61 is not the cheapest way in, and we cannot say which tier the sign-up page had preselected.

The mail timeline further down lists two vendor emails from 21 and 24 November 2026. Salesmsg told us on 25 November 2026 that the 21 November email, 'Your Salesmsg account is almost ready', is a follow-up it sends to incomplete sign-ups. Read the timeline that way: it is not evidence that an account was opened, because none was.
